rationale: Request the execution of a dedicated basis for the PreVote scenario: it now has its own self-contained harness so that every alias's event appears exactly once, after the four-scenario basis left its comparisons unknown. The verified native run shows the source-predicted sequence (stale answer before the tick, a follower with no leader after one tick, no answer afterwards), and the comparisons are the two premises, the pre-step-down witness, the one-tick bound and the post-step-down drop.

experiment.revision_reason: The PreVote scenario now has its own self-contained harness and its own comparisons instead of sharing one prerequisite set with the other three scenarios, because the four-scenario basis left its new comparisons unknown (missing indices pointing at unmatched events of the last scenario). The harness contains only the PreVote scenario and copies the helpers it needs, so each alias's event appears exactly once.

scope.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path when only PreVote is enabled: the same three-voter removal leaves a single-voter configuration, the remaining voter becomes leader and commits an entry, the removed leader answers a read before its next heartbeat tick, and the observations continue after that tick.
assumptions: Three voters {1,2,3} with PreVote enabled on every node and CheckQuorum disabled; node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, and node 2 then becomes leader of {2} and commits one entry.
The read is delivered to node 1 before it has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered to node 1 and its messages are pumped, and then a second read is delivered.

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 in {1,2,3} with a real MsgHup/MsgVote round, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all nodes, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, deliver one heartbeat tick of node 1 and pump its messages, then deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely). The tracker's own comment for IsSingleton says the single voting member is the leader, so answering locally without any check is only sound when that member is the local node.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and message handling decides whether the removed leader learns of the new term.

comparisons.description: Premise: with PreVote enabled the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2.
Premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Witness before the step-down: with PreVote only, the removed leader answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
Bound: one heartbeat tick is enough for the step-down, matching the guard (checkQuorum || preVote) on messages from a lower term.
After the step-down the same request is no longer answered, so PreVote alone bounds the exposure.
